title: WHY BEZALEL WAS FILLED WITH THE SPIRIT BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING
paragraphs: WHY BEZALEL WAS FILLED WITH THE SPIRIT BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING
The scandal is not that God uses broken people.
The scandal is that God often fills people before anyone else sees what they are capable of doing.
Long before the tabernacle stood in the wilderness.
Long before the curtains were woven.
Long before Israel could point to anything impressive and say, “Look what God has done.”
There was a man named Bezalel.
Yet Scripture quietly reveals something astonishing about him.
God filled him with His Spirit before he built anything.
Because we live in a world obsessed with visible results.
We praise what can be measured.
But heaven often starts somewhere completely different.
Before God ever measures what a person creates, He looks at who they are becoming.
That is where the story of Bezalel begins.

“See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with ability and intelligence, with knowledge and all craftsmanship…”
God did not say, “Bezalel proved himself, so I filled him.”
God did not say, “Bezalel became famous, so I empowered him.”
God did not say, “Bezalel built something extraordinary, therefore My Spirit came upon him.”
The phrase translated “I have filled him” comes from the Hebrew verb מָלֵא (male’), meaning “to fill completely,” “to make full,” or “to saturate.”
God is not describing a small blessing.
Bezalel was not merely assisted by God.
The text says he was filled with רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים (Ruach Elohim) — “the Spirit of God.”
The same Spirit present in creation.
The same Spirit hovering over the waters in Genesis 1:2.
The same Spirit who empowers prophets.
The same Spirit who would later descend upon believers through Christ.
The first person explicitly described in Scripture as being filled with the Spirit is not a prophet.
Someone whose calling involved his hands.
That should stop every believer in their tracks.
Because many Christians secretly divide life into “spiritual work” and “ordinary work.”
The God who inspired sermons also inspired craftsmanship.
The God who anointed prophets also anointed artists.
The God who empowered apostles also empowered builders.
The tabernacle was not a side project.
It was the dwelling place of God's presence among His people.
Every detail pointed toward something greater.
Ultimately, every detail pointed toward Christ.
The tabernacle itself was a prophetic masterpiece.
Every element whispered the name of Jesus centuries before Bethlehem.
When God filled Bezalel, He was not merely constructing furniture.
He was building shadows that would eventually find their substance in Christ.
“For the law has but a shadow of the good things to come.” (Hebrews 10:1)
Bezalel's craftsmanship became prophecy in wood, gold, silver, fabric, and stone.
His work helped people see what was coming.
Yet there is something even deeper happening beneath the surface.
The meaning of Bezalel's name is remarkable.
בְּצַלְאֵל (Beṣalʾel) is commonly understood as “In the shadow of God.”
The man who would construct the place where God would dwell among His people carried a name that meant living under God's shadow.
Nothing about this story feels accidental.
God filled him with His Spirit.
God empowered him before anyone applauded him.
How many believers today are waiting for recognition before embracing their calling?
How many are delaying obedience because nobody notices them?
How many think significance begins when people finally pay attention?
Bezalel reminds us that heaven's approval always comes before earthly applause.
God knew his name before Israel knew his work.
And perhaps that is exactly where some readers find themselves today.
Because God often develops the vessel before displaying the assignment.
The greatest danger is not being unseen by people.
The greatest danger is being seen by people before being prepared by God.
Bezalel received something many modern believers desperately need.
The Hebrew text says God gave him wisdom, understanding, and knowledge.
תְּבוּנָה (tevunah) refers to discernment and understanding.
Because excellence can be an act of worship.
That truth should transform how believers view every assignment.
Every calling becomes holy when surrendered to Christ.
The Gospel destroys the false divide between sacred and secular.
Jesus is Lord over all of it.
And perhaps this is where the story becomes deeply personal.
Many people spend years trying to build something impressive for God.
But Bezalel teaches a different lesson.
God is more interested in filling you than displaying you.
More interested in transforming you than promoting you.
More interested in your surrender than your success.
The greatest masterpiece God was building was never the tabernacle.
And the same remains true today.
Before God builds through you, He wants to work within you.
Before He entrusts influence, He develops intimacy.
Before He gives visibility, He teaches dependency.
Before He displays His power, He forms Christ within you.
This is where the Gospel shines brightest.
Because none of us arrive qualified.
The greatest scandal in human history is not that humanity failed.
The greatest scandal is that God loved humanity anyway.
And now offers grace freely to all who believe.
The Greek word χάρις (charis), translated “grace,” means unearned favor.
The cross forever declares that God's love is not based on our performance.
It is rooted in His character.
That means your identity is not your accomplishments.
Your identity is not your failures.
Your identity is not your past.
Your identity is found in Christ.
And when Christ rewrites a life, everything changes.
That is the heartbeat of Bezalel's story.
And it is the heartbeat of our story too.
This may have touched a place you have not allowed anyone else to see.
Your support helps make possible the continued creation of Scripture-rich content that points people to Christ and helps them grow deeper in His Word.
Because one day, when all earthly achievements fade, the greatest question will not be what you built.
It will be whether you allowed God to fill you.
And sometimes the holiest thing God is building is the person nobody notices yet.
